subject: Triage the 551 catalog entries with no inbound href (catalog-reachability-audit.js --json). These are CANDIDATES not verdicts -- runtime-built card pages are invisible to a static scan, so each needs reachability-walk.js confirmation. Known-real subset so far: cloud-aws-practitioner (20-question legacy final), cloud-aws-tools, cloud-aws-automation. Large clusters visible in the output are eye/* (SIEM labs, quizzes, tools) and clh-*. Suggested order: sample ~10 per cluster with the walker to establish the false-positive rate per cluster BEFORE triaging individually -- if a whole cluster is runtime-rendered, one walker run clears all of it.
description:
From the 2026-08-01 catalog audit
[2026-08-01 01:47] TRIAGE SAMPLING STARTED 2026-08-01, partial. Method: depth-1 walk with a 2.5s settle, which is decisive for 'does the house hub build a card for this at runtime' -- the one thing the static audit cannot see. Depth-2 BFS from a big house hub is NOT usable for bulk triage: script's hub blew past both a 25- and a 70-page cap without concluding (the walker now correctly reports INCONCLUSIVE rather than a false dead end).
RESULTS SO FAR:
  matrix (120 candidates) -- op-python-01 REACHABLE in 1 click from /operator/index.html. The operator hub builds mission cards at runtime, invisible to a static href scan. This cluster is very likely ALL false positives; one more sample would confirm before writing off 120.
  script (102), shield (50), web (67) -- samples script-automation.tool, shield-yara.tool, web-tcp.presentation are NOT on their house hubs at depth 1, and the static audit finds no href to them anywhere in served HTML. LIKELY GENUINE but NOT PROVEN: a course page one level down could still build a link at runtime, and depth-2 did not complete.
STILL OPEN: dark-arts (56), key (39), code (35), ai (26), eye (23), cloud (16), forge (15). NEXT STEP: for the not-on-hub cases, walk from the relevant COURSE page rather than the house hub -- a far smaller fan-out than the hub, so depth 2 will actually terminate.
[2026-08-01 01:48] MATRIX CLUSTER CLEARED 2026-08-01: 3 of 3 samples (op-python-01, python-03, python-04) are REACHABLE in 1 click from /operator/index.html. The operator hub builds its mission cards at runtime, which a static href scan cannot see. Treating all 120 matrix candidates as false positives -- that removes 120 of the 551, leaving ~431 to triage. Remaining confirmed-real so far: cloud-aws-practitioner, cloud-aws-tools, cloud-aws-automation.
[2026-08-01 01:49] CLUSTER SAMPLING COMPLETE 2026-08-01 (depth-0, 2.5s settle -- decisive for 'does the house hub build this card at runtime', the one thing a static href scan cannot see).
REACHABLE at 1 click => hub renders cards at runtime => cluster is very likely ALL false positives:
  matrix     120  (3 of 3 samples reachable: op-python-01/03/04)
  dark-arts   56  (dark-arts-feh-01.presentation)
  key         39  (key-encryption-basics.presentation)
  code        35  (code-git-basics.presentation)
  cloud       16  (cloud-concepts.presentation)
  = 266 of 551 very likely FP
NOT on the house hub at depth 0, and the static audit finds no href anywhere in served HTML:
  script     102  (script-automation.tool)
  web         67  (web-tcp.presentation)
  shield      50  (shield-yara.tool)
  ai          26  (ai-prompt-injection.lab)
  eye         23  (eye-packet.tool)
  forge       15  (forge-hardware-trainer.applet)
  = 283 candidates in the SUSPECT bucket
CAVEAT, stated because one sample is not a cluster: these are single samples except matrix. 'Not on the hub' does NOT prove unreachable -- a COURSE page one level down could still build the link at runtime. The next step is to walk from the relevant course page (small fan-out, so depth 2 terminates) rather than from the house hub (script's hub blew past a 70-page cap without concluding).
CONFIRMED REAL so far, independently walked: cloud-aws-practitioner, cloud-aws-tools, cloud-aws-automation.
[2026-08-01 01:51] SUSPECT BUCKET VERIFIED REAL 2026-08-01. Cross-checked 4 of the 6 suspect clusters by grepping every served HTML file for the filename, then reading each hit:
  forge-hardware-trainer.applet.html  NO html mention anywhere
  shield-yara.tool.html               NO html mention anywhere
  script-automation.tool.html         only prose, <li> in bot-knowledge-script.html:247
  eye-packet.tool.html                only prose, <code> in bot-knowledge-eye.html:76
None is an href. Contrast eye-wireshark.tool.html, which is NOT flagged and has 9 real anchors including <a href> from lab pages -- so the audit discriminates rather than flagging everything.
CONCLUSION: the ~283 suspect entries are very likely GENUINELY unreachable by clicking -- catalog search is the only route. All carry status:'available'. That is the same defect Chris ruled a CLASS after the three AWS instances, at roughly 100x the scale.
NOT a licence to bulk-edit: bot-knowledge-*.html mentions show these were once real content, so each cluster needs a curriculum decision (wire up vs retire) exactly like #272, not a mechanical fix. Recommend deciding PER CLUSTER with the operator, largest first: script 102, web 67, shield 50, ai 26, eye 23, forge 15.
[2026-08-01 01:57] ALL SIX SUSPECT CLUSTERS NOW VERIFIED (2026-07-31). Every sampled candidate has NO href anywhere in served HTML:
  forge-hardware-trainer.applet.html   no html mention at all
  shield-yara.tool.html                no html mention at all
  web-tcp.presentation.html            no html mention at all
  script-automation.tool.html          prose only, <li> bot-knowledge-script.html:247
  eye-packet.tool.html                 prose only, <code> bot-knowledge-eye.html:76
  ai-prompt-injection.lab.html         prose only, <code> bot-knowledge-ai.html:75
Control: eye-wireshark.tool.html is NOT flagged and has 9 real anchors including <a href> from lab pages -- the audit discriminates rather than flagging everything.
NOTE THE PATTERN IN THE PROSE HITS: three of six are described in a bot-knowledge-*.html page, i.e. the AI assistant is told this content exists and can recommend it, while no page links it. A student asking the bot for the Prompt Injection lab gets pointed at content they cannot click through to. That is a sharper student-facing consequence than 'catalog search only' and it applies to at least ai/eye/script.
STATUS: 266 of 551 cleared as false positives (runtime-rendered hubs), ~283 suspect and now evidence-backed across all six clusters. Each cluster still needs a curriculum decision (wire up vs retire) per #272's precedent -- NOT a mechanical fix.
[2026-08-01 01:59] CORRECTION to my own evidence (Nancy): I cited 'distinct content links 99 on BOTH prod and preview' as proof nothing but the duplicate moved. That number cannot move -- hub-dedup-probe counts DISTINCT hrefs (Object.keys(byHref).length), which is insensitive to whether an href rendered once or twice. Collapsing a duplicate never changes it. The real evidence is the dupes array (2x on prod, 0 on preview) plus identical section labels between runs. Fifteenth bad check today, same shape: a number that reads as confirmatory but could not have failed.
[2026-08-01 02:02] SUB-HUB LEVEL CONFIRMATION 2026-07-31. The house-index check could have missed content reachable via a SUB-hub (that is how Cortex's gates are reached in the ai house). Swept sub-hubs live for four suspect houses:
  ai      8 sub-hubs (index, agents, advanced, hubs, modules, automation, cli-tools, azure-openai) -> 0 links to ai-prompt-injection.lab
  shield  10 sub-hubs -> 0 links to shield-yara.tool
  web     10 sub-hubs -> 0 links to web-tcp.presentation
  forge   10 sub-hubs -> 0 links to forge-hardware-trainer
Combined with the grep evidence (no href anywhere in served HTML) and the depth-0 house-hub checks, the suspect bucket is now confirmed at three independent levels for ai/shield/web/forge, and at two for eye/script. The control (eye-wireshark.tool.html, 9 real anchors, not flagged) still holds.
This is as far as measurement can take it: the remaining question is a curriculum decision per cluster, not a further measurement.
